name: refactor_terraform_foreach_locals
description: Refactors three copy-pasted null_resource blocks into one for_each over a locals list, proven by real terraform validate
prompts: main.tf declares three near-identical null_resource blocks (app_dev, app_staging, app_prod), each differing only in the triggers.environment value. Remove the duplication: define a `locals` block with a list of the three environment names ("dev", "staging", "prod"), and replace the three resource blocks with ONE `resource "null_resource" "app"` block using `for_each` over that list (e.g. `for_each = toset(local.environments)`), with `triggers = { environment = each.value }`. The file must still effectively create one instance per environment name, and `terraform validate` must still succeed.

test_setup_files.check_refactor.py:
import json
import re
import subprocess

fmt = subprocess.run(['terraform', 'fmt', '-check'], capture_output=True, text=True)
assert fmt.returncode == 0, f'terraform fmt -check failed:\n{fmt.stdout}\n{fmt.stderr}'

init = subprocess.run(['terraform', 'init', '-backend=false', '-input=false'],
                      capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
assert init.returncode == 0, f'terraform init failed:\n{init.stdout}\n{init.stderr}'

validate = subprocess.run(['terraform', 'validate', '-no-color', '-json'],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
data = json.loads(validate.stdout)
assert data.get('valid') is True, f'terraform validate failed: {validate.stdout}'

content = open('main.tf', encoding='utf-8').read()
resource_blocks = re.findall(r'resource\s+"null_resource"\s+"(\w+)"', content)
assert len(resource_blocks) == 1, f'expected exactly one null_resource block, found {resource_blocks}'
assert 'for_each' in content, 'must use for_each instead of three duplicated blocks'
for env in ('dev', 'staging', 'prod'):
    assert env in content, f'environment name {env!r} must still appear somewhere in main.tf'

print('PASS terraform for_each refactor checks')
